hero.oneLiner: An Indian pharmaceutical company engaged in large-scale manufacturing and supply of generic medicines to government institutions under a business-to-government (B2G) framework.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: An Indian pharmaceutical company engaged in large-scale manufacturing and supply of generic medicines to government institutions under a business-to-government (B2G) framework.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies generic formulations - medicines whose patents have expired - primarily under procurement contracts won through competitive tenders for central government projects under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through GoI agencies and state government agencies or bodies. Products are supplied either under brand names or generic names and, save for those manufactured for others, carry the Company's logo. It supplied products across India to 27 States and Union Territories in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and to 27 States and Union Territories in Fiscal 2025.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Integrated formulation manufacturing at a single Palghar site: the Company manufactures multiple dosage forms (tablets, capsules, sachets, bottles, external liquids, creams, aerosols, ointments, combination blister packages and external powders) in-house, and describes a versatile facility able to produce multiple products using a combination of processes, allowing the product mix to be changed in response to changes in market demand. Quality control is in-house: the quality control department has the responsibility and authority to approve or reject raw materials, packaging components, intermediate materials, in-process materials, semi-finished products and finished products. Inputs are bought in rather than backward-integrated; cost of material consumed (raw materials plus packing materials) was 48.15% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 51.79%, 51.83% and 57.03% of total expenses in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. The Company states it has no long-term contracts with its third-party suppliers; prices are negotiated for each purchase order and it generally has more than one supplier for each raw material. It also purchases stock-in-trade (trading goods purchases of Rs 110.43 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and Rs 194.45 million and Rs 33.43 million in Fiscals 2025 and 2024). Downstream, the Palghar facility is equipped with a warehouse; products are sold on a Cost and Freight (CnF) basis; the Company owns no vehicles for transportation and relies on third-party transportation and logistics providers, with finished goods shipped through freight forwarders appointed by the Company or nominated by customers. Freight charges were 2.43% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 2.93%, 2.78% and 2.48% in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. Route to market is direct tender-based supply to Government Customers, handled by a dedicated tendering team of 8 personnel as of September 30, 2025; no distributor or retail channel layer is described.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue concentration in tender-based sales to Government Customers (approximately 90% of revenue from operations across the reported periods), so revenue depends on acceptance of bids submitted in competitive procurement processes
- Lengthening working capital cycle - Net Working Capital Days rose from 52 in Fiscal 2023 to 78 in Fiscal 2024, 115 in Fiscal 2025 and 133 in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Receivables extension - Debtor Days of 97 (Fiscal 2023), 92 (Fiscal 2024), 97 (Fiscal 2025) and 124 in the six months ended September 30, 2025; Creditor Days compressed from 52 (Fiscal 2023) to 20 (Fiscal 2025) and 26 in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Margin expansion - EBITDA margin moved from 17.81% in Fiscal 2023 to 23.66% in Fiscal 2024 and 24.52% in Fiscal 2025, with 22.60% in the six months ended September 30, 2025; PAT margin moved from 12.91% to 18.78% over Fiscal 2023 to Fiscal 2025
- Therapeutic mix shift - Antiparasitic fell from 13.06% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 0.08% in the six months ended September 30, 2025 while Blood Related rose to 22.70% and Keratolytic rose from 2.98% to 6.67% over the same span
- Emerging private-customer channel - private customer revenue rose from 0.21% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 9.17% in Fiscal 2025 and 10.07% in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Low leverage - Debt/Equity of 0.01 (Fiscal 2023), 0.08 (Fiscal 2024), 0.06 (Fiscal 2025) and 0.04 at the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Competition and pricing - the Company competes on product portfolio, quality and regulatory compliance, on-time delivery and manufacturing flexibility, and cost-effective manufacturing; competition may result in a decrease in the price paid for its products and services

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Add Unit 2 at the existing Palghar manufacturing facility to increase capacity
- Add cosmetics production at Unit 2
- Expand the generic formulations business internationally to supply foreign government customers (not including the United States)
- Continue to focus on supplying products to Government Customers through the tendering process, leveraging accumulated understanding of public procurement policies, regulatory frameworks and quality assurance requirements
- Continue expanding the breadth of the generic formulation product portfolio and dosage forms offered to Government Customers

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is adding a Unit 2 at its existing Palghar, Maharashtra manufacturing facility to increase capacity. Unit 2 will be 2,842 square meters and is expected to have an installed annual capacity of 2,500 million tablets, 30 million bottles of external liquids, 17.50 million bottles of ointments and 15 million jars of creams. The Company also plans to add cosmetics production at Unit 2. Unit 2 has been constructed and an application has been made for the required licenses; it is under commissioning and production is yet to commence. Separately, the Company states as a business strategy that it plans to expand its generic formulations business internationally to supply foreign government customers, not including the United States.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Well placed to leverage its position in the generic supply segment, with a dedicated focus of supplying to Government Customers - sales to Government Customers contributed approximately 90% of revenue in each of the six months ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023
- Track record of successful tenders for procurement contracts with Government Customers - win ratio of 78.57% in the six months ended September 30, 2025, 63.95% in Fiscal 2025, 59.60% in Fiscal 2024 and 69.70% in Fiscal 2023; pre-qualification criteria are stated to provide an advantage over new entrants
- Large, diversified and fast-growing generic formulation product portfolio - grew from 661 products as of March 31, 2023 to 871 products as of March 31, 2025 and 948 products as of September 30, 2025, spanning acute and chronic therapeutic segments
- Extensive and diversified manufacturing capabilities supported by quality focused processes
- Demonstrated growth, profitability and capital efficiency
- Experienced Promoters and Senior Management with strong industry expertise
- In-house tendering team within the business development department that identifies, reviews and evaluates procurement opportunities using a frequently updated risk management matrix

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Revenue concentration on tender-based sales to Government Customers — Government Customers contributed approximately 90% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and in Fiscal 2025 (98.14% in Fiscal 2024 and 99.79% in Fiscal 2023). Revenues depend on the acceptance of bids submitted for meeting procurement requirements; projects are awarded through competitive bidding and satisfaction of prescribed pre-qualification criteria.
- Bid win ratio is variable and a portion of bids remains undecided — Win ratio was 69.70% in Fiscal 2023, 59.60% in Fiscal 2024, 63.95% in Fiscal 2025 and 78.57% in the six months ended September 30, 2025; in the six months ended September 30, 2025 there were 20 further bids where results were still awaited.
- Highly competitive and fragmented market — The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented with over 10,000 manufacturers in the organised and unorganised sectors, and approximately 8,000 SMEs make up about 70% of total pharmaceutical units. Some competitors may have substantially greater financial, marketing, technical or other resources; competition may decrease the price paid for the Company's products and services.
- Working capital intensity and lengthening receivables cycle — Net Working Capital Days rose from 52 in Fiscal 2023 to 115 in Fiscal 2025 and 133 in the six months ended September 30, 2025, with Debtor Days at 124 in the six months ended September 30, 2025 while Creditor Days compressed to 26. ₹725.00 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for funding working capital requirements.
- Single manufacturing location — Manufacturing is situated at one site at Palghar, Maharashtra (Unit 1, with Unit 2 being added at the same existing facility), concentrating operational, regulatory and licensing exposure at one location.
- Unit 2 commissioning and licensing execution — Unit 2 has been constructed and an application has been made for the required licenses, but it is under commissioning and production is yet to commence, so the stated incremental annual capacity is not yet operating.
- Planned international expansion introduces new competitive and execution exposure — The Company states that as it commences international business it expects competition from major international generic manufacturers, and flags that failure to manage the risks associated with exporting products internationally may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and future prospects.
- Reliance on operational metrics tracked with internal systems and tools — Non-GAAP measures, industry metrics and key performance indicators presented are subject to inherent measurement challenges, are not required by Ind AS, and may not be comparable with similarly named measures of other companies.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Commission Unit 2 at the existing Palghar, Maharashtra manufacturing facility, which has been constructed with licence applications made and is under commissioning with production yet to commence.**
- **Unit 2 is expected to have an installed annual capacity of 30 million bottles of external liquids, 17.50 million bottles of ointments and 15 million jars of creams.**
- **Add cosmetics production at Unit 2.**
- **Expand the generic formulations business internationally to supply foreign government customers, not including the United States.**
- **Deploy Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue towards funding the working capital requirements of the Company.**
- **General corporate purposes, with the amount to be utilised for general corporate purposes not exceeding 25% of the Gross Proceeds in accordance with the SEBI ICDR Regulations.**
- **Continue to focus on supplying products to Government Customers through the tender process across central and state government departments and agencies.**
- **Continue expanding the generic formulation product portfolio, which grew from 661 products as of March 31, 2023 to 871 products as of March 31, 2025 and 948 products as of September 30, 2025.**
- **Management flags that as it commences its international business it expects competition from major international generic manufacturers, and that failure to manage export-related risks may adversely affect the business.**
- **Management flags that revenues depend on the acceptance of bids submitted for meeting the procurement requirements of Government Customers, awarded through competitive bidding and satisfaction of prescribed pre-qualification criteria.**
